================================================================================
EGZOS — DECISIONS LOG · v0.7 AMENDMENT SET
Delta on top of the v0.4 log and the v0.5 and v0.6 amendment sets. Records
the Chief's calls of 2026-10-22/23: buy, don't build; Supabase for the
platform services; one login; the Face ID / Touch ID confirm; places and
git-like sync; the egzosux experience; Stripe; the repository's visibility.
Sections not mentioned carry forward unchanged. Compiled 2026-10-23.
Read together with: egzos-decisions-log-v0.4.txt · egzos-decisions-v0.5-
amendments.txt · egzos-decisions-v0.6-amendments.txt · egzos-handoff.txt ·
egzos-build-plan-v1.2.txt
================================================================================

Status key:  [DECIDED] locked · [LEAN] stated preference, not locked ·
             [LATER] decided in direction, not scheduled ·
             [OPEN→CHIEF] explicitly awaiting the Chief's call


================================================================================
R. BUY, DON'T BUILD (new; binds every agent and the operator)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] IF A WIDELY USED SERVICE OR LIBRARY DOES THE JOB, WE USE IT. Login,
          OAuth, sessions, passkeys, databases, file storage, payments,
          hosting, DNS, email, queues, cloud-storage connectors and crypto
          primitives are bought (a paid service, or a maintained open-source
          project), never built. We build only what egzos IS: the node model
          and resolver, the trust rules and the gate, the ledger, the
          container contract, sync between places, and the experience.

[DECIDED] BUILDING A COMMODITY PIECE NEEDS THE CHIEF'S EXPLICIT YES, recorded
          in this log. An issue or PR that would build one says so in its
          first line and names the service it passed over and why. A review
          that finds commodity infrastructure built without that record
          raises it as a finding.

[DECIDED] Recorded as the reason for this rule: the container's own OAuth 2.1
          authorization server (§K, v0.6) was built slice by slice for
          weeks without the build-or-buy question being put to the Chief.
          It is retired in §S.


================================================================================
S. PLATFORM SERVICES — SUPABASE (supersedes v0.6 §K's own-AS decision;
   amends v0.5 §C and R3's "server-side stack chosen at Phase 6")
================================================================================

[DECIDED] SUPABASE IS THE ONE VENDOR for everything it covers:
          - login (Supabase Auth);
          - agent sign-in: Supabase's OAuth 2.1 server issues MCP clients
            their tokens (PKCE, dynamic client registration); egzos.io hosts
            the consent page it redirects to;
          - the hosted database (Postgres);
          - file storage (Supabase Storage: S3-compatible, signed URLs,
            files up to 500 GB on paid plans);
          - server-side glue such as payment webhooks (Edge Functions).
          Self-hosters run the open-source Supabase for the same parts.

[DECIDED] THE CONTAINER'S OWN AUTHORIZATION SERVER IS RETIRED. No further
          slices. authorization-server.md leaves the contract set; the
          unmounted code under src/egzos/authz/** is removed in the PR that
          lands Supabase token verification. Device-code for the CLI is
          retired with it: the CLI keeps its local token, and signs in to a
          cloud through Supabase.

[DECIDED] THE CONTAINER IS A RESOURCE SERVER. It verifies Supabase-issued
          JWTs (issuer, signature against the project's published keys,
          expiry) and maps them to a principal:
          - a user session (no client) → principal: interactive, with the
            role the container grants that user;
          - an OAuth-issued agent token → principal: client, with the role
            and scopes the container's agent registry grants that client.
          Supabase does not bind tokens to a resource (no RFC 8707), so the
          container also checks the client against its own registry; an
          unregistered client is refused like any unknown token (silence-
          not-errors holds).

[DECIDED] LOCALS STAY LOCAL. A local container keeps SQLite, the blob store
          on disk, its local token, MCP over stdio, and works offline. The
          Supabase parts serve clouds and the sign-in to them.

[DECIDED] STORAGE BACKENDS SIT BEHIND APACHE OpenDAL (one library for local
          disk, S3 and Supabase Storage today, and Azure Blob, GCS and the
          rest for §V's Cloud 2), not one adapter per provider.

[LEAN]    HOSTING for the hosted container: a managed host (Fly.io), with
          Cloudflare for DNS. Accounts and payment are the Chief's.


================================================================================
T. ONE LOGIN (supersedes R2 and v0.6 §K "two authorities")
================================================================================

[DECIDED] LOGGING IN TO egzos.io IS LOGGING IN TO YOUR CONTAINER. The
          container trusts the egzos Supabase project as its identity
          provider, and the browser presents the user's Supabase session to
          the container directly. Double login is retired.

[DECIDED] Accepted tradeoff, on record: the egzos Supabase project can now
          sign a session the user's container accepts, so egzos's identity
          provider is in the trust path of every container that uses it. A
          container owner can point the container at a different identity
          provider (a self-hoster's own Supabase); egzos's is the default.

[DECIDED] What stays: the browser talks to the container directly. egzos
          servers never proxy, cache or store a user's container data, and
          never call a user's container on their own authority. For a
          bring-your-own container the data plane still never touches egzos
          servers.


================================================================================
U. THE CONFIRM — FACE ID / TOUCH ID (amends R11's step-up and v0.6 §K's
   presence LEAN; closes v0.6 open question 6)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] A MOVE OR COPY THAT CHANGES WHO CAN SEE SOMETHING ASKS RIGHT THERE,
          inline: who will newly see it, then confirm. No separate page, no
          localhost tap window.

[DECIDED] THE CONFIRM IS THE DEVICE'S OWN BIOMETRIC: Face ID, Touch ID or
          Windows Hello, through WebAuthn with user verification required.
          Where the device has none, a plain confirm button. The audit event
          records which proof was given (biometric or button), so the ledger
          shows the weaker one for what it is. The button is a human act: it
          is refused to an agent's token (principal: client), so an agent
          driving a browser cannot confirm on the human's behalf.

[DECIDED] BUILT ON ESTABLISHED PIECES (§R): the browser's WebAuthn API and a
          maintained WebAuthn library to verify the assertion, or Supabase
          Auth's own WebAuthn support where it covers re-verification. No
          home-made challenge protocol.

[LATER]   PASSKEY SIGN-IN as an opt-in (Supabase Auth passkeys, in beta
          since May 2026).

[DECIDED] The step-up window (R11, ≈5 minutes per ring pair) carries over to
          the confirm unchanged.


================================================================================
V. PLACES AND SYNC (new; amends the storage contract at the next contract
   version)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] A CONTAINER HAS PLACES: one hosted cloud and any number of locals
          (a laptop, a desktop). Each project has a home place.

[DECIDED] SYNC IS GIT-LIKE, NOT LIVE: a local pushes what it has and pulls
          ("catches up") what it lacks, when asked; `status` says what is
          ahead and behind. Each place keeps its own ledger, and a push is
          verified on arrival (its hash chain) before it lands.

[DECIDED] COPY JOINS MOVE as a verb. Both run the gate: a copy that widens
          the audience is confirmed exactly like a move (§U).

[DECIDED] ORDER: one hosted cloud plus locals that push and pull come first.

[LATER]   CLOUD 2 — BRING YOUR OWN CLOUD: a user enters connection details
          for their own Azure, AWS or other storage, and it appears as a
          space they can upload into and import from, without an agent (the
          Chief's work Azure environment is the first case). Cloud
          containers become multi-backend. Built on OpenDAL (§S).

[LATER]   THE RELAY AND LIVE SYNC as an opt-in for users who want continuous
          sync. The idea is kept; it is not scheduled.


================================================================================
W. THE EXPERIENCE — egzosux (amends R3, R10 and §P of v0.6)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] THE egzosux PROTOTYPE (Egzos/egzosux) IS THE EXPERIENCE SPEC, SET
          BY THE CHIEF. Binding as experience, not as final visuals:
          - a 3D space; clouds and locals (locals as houses); the egzos orb,
            the ether that content sinks into; agents as pyramids;
          - navigation cloud → project → thread → artifacts;
          - move or copy an artifact to another thread, another project, or
            loose in a project;
          - XR.
          It supersedes the flagship's 2D screen specs as the flow; visual
          direction stays open and keeps flowing through the tokens.

[DECIDED] THE BUILT-IN CURATOR AGENT IS J4S (short for Jarvis), not "Chief".
          "Chief" names the human gate only.

[DECIDED] STACK (amends R3): TypeScript, three.js on its WebGL renderer
          (WebGPU is not used), React for the panels, Vite 8, WebXR. Tailwind
          and the tokens for the panels' chrome.

[DECIDED] ALL FRONT-END WORK LIVES IN Egzos/egzos-platform. egzosux stays the
          reference prototype; nothing is built on it in place. One component
          set, one tokens file, consistent and standardized across screens.

[DECIDED] THE egzos.io HOMEPAGE HOSTS THE EXPERIENCE AS A LIVE DEMO, on
          sample data, that a visitor can use before signing up. The
          homepage is decluttered and built on the same stack and the same
          3D code as the app, so the demo and the product cannot drift. The
          old demo site is replaced, not restyled.


================================================================================
X. BILLING — STRIPE BEHIND A PROVIDER INTERFACE (amends v0.5 §C)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] STRIPE handles payments: Stripe Checkout to subscribe, the Stripe
          customer portal to manage, webhooks into Supabase. egzos builds no
          payment form or invoice screen that Stripe already hosts.

[DECIDED] egzos code talks to a payments-provider interface, not to Stripe
          directly, so a second provider can be added later without
          rewriting billing.


================================================================================
Y. REPOSITORY VISIBILITY AND DISCLOSURE (amends v0.6 §L)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Egzos/egzos IS PUBLIC AGAIN (the Chief, 2026-10-23), after a
          private interval in October 2026. §L's disclosure mechanics apply
          again: unfixed security findings are private GitHub Security
          Advisories; the regression test enters adversarial/ only in the
          fix PR. Egzos/egzos-platform stays private; its security findings
          stay issues there (its CLAUDE.md).


================================================================================
Z. RETENTION — NO AUTOMATIC DELETION (amends R11's staged-blob retention)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Nothing is deleted automatically when a retention period ends.
          Staged bytes past retention are surfaced to their owner, who
          keeps or purges them. R11's "30 days cold, then purge" becomes
          "30 days, then ask."

[LATER]   AUTO-FILING: egzos files incoming content for the user. Wanted as
          an extension of the system; not built now.


================================================================================
AA. AMENDMENT — EVERY TOKEN IS BOUND TO ONE CONTAINER (amends §S's mapping
    "a user session (no client) → principal: interactive" and §T's "the
    browser presents the user's Supabase session to the container
    directly"; Egzos/egzos#282)
================================================================================

[DECIDED] Recorded 2026-10-23 by the operator, under the Chief's standing
          instruction to run the build, on a1r's and a6's review of #282;
          the Chief may veto. Why: a provider session is valid at every
          container that trusts the provider, so a container that received
          a person's session could present it at another container the
          same person can reach.

[DECIDED] No container accepts a bare provider session. Each container is
          a public OAuth client of the provider; a person reaches it with a
          token the provider's OAuth 2.1 server issued to that container's
          client (PKCE), and an agent with a token issued to a client
          registered on that container. A token bound to one container is
          refused at every other.

[DECIDED] What does not change: one sign-in covers every container — no
          second password, no second login (§T). egzos.io obtains each
          container's token for the person through the provider; the
          consent page approves a person's own containers without asking
          again. Principal: the container's own client → interactive; a
          registered agent client → client. Contract: identity.md §3a.
